Cerberus. The three-headed monstrous hound of the underworld who stood guard at the gates of Hades, ensuring that no living soul could pass and no dead soul could escape. He possessed three massive dog heads, each capable of independent action and fury, allowing him to watch in all directions simultaneously. His tail was said to be a serpent itself, coiling and striking at intruders, making him part hound and part serpent composite.

Cerberus was not evil by nature but served his master Hades faithfully, showing mercy only to those who came willingly to the underworld. The musician Orpheus famously charmed all three heads with his lyre, the only living mortal known to have pacified the beast through art rather than force. Heracles, however, subdued him through strength and determination, wrestling the hound without weapons and bringing it to the surface as proof of his twelfth labor. His parentage was often given as Typhon and Echidna, making him kin to the Chimera and Lernaean Hydra. After Heracles displayed him to King Eurystheus as evidence of his final labor, the beast was safely returned to the underworld, where he resumed his eternal post. The very presence of Cerberus was said to instill dread in mortals; even seeing a representation of him could inspire terror.
